newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn mulls giving Thyssen-Krupp aid for job cuts.
newsitem.headline: Bonn mulls giving Thyssen-Krupp aid for job cuts.

text.p: The German government is to decide in the coming weeks whether to give aid to Thyssen and Krupp to finance job cuts when they merge their carbon steel operations, company officials said on Thursday.

Ekkehard Schulz, the designated chairman of the new merged steel venture Thyssen Krupp Stahl AG KFHG.F, told reporters after a news conference that he was hopeful Bonn would provide aid to cushion the restructuring costs associated with the merger.
"We hope Bonn will decide in the next few weeks," he said on the sidelines of a news conference, but gave no details about the amount of aid or its purpose.
In the past, Bonn has helped steel companies by providing assistance in early retirement payments or granting funds for infrastructure improvements.
Dieter Henning, the labour representative on Thyssen AG's management board, said: "There are talks with politicians in Bonn, but there are still no results."
Thyssen and Fried. Krupp AG Hoesch-Krupp agreed this week to merge their carbon steel activities into a new company called Thyssen Krupp Stahl AG.
The new company will begin operating on April 1. Thyssen will hold a majority of 60 percent and Krupp will hold a 40 percent share.
The steel merger follows Krupp's failed hostile takeover bid for the entire Thyssen group that was launched last week and withdrawn on Monday.
